summary: Parallel subsystem survey to build a verified project handoff/state doc

surveys.subsystem: kernel (src/nbb_cp/kernel/) — the pure, stdlib-only decision core of the NBB Control Plane
surveys.one_liner: A dependency-free "decides but never acts" core: 12 numbered invariants, fail-closed frozen domain types (integer-cents Money, five-state revenue, Proposal/Verdict), pure gate functions that are the only enforcement primitives, an append-only hash-chained ledger, and a runtime audit that re-checks the state-verifiable invariants — all effects pushed out behind Protocol ports.

key_files.role: The 12-invariant registry (INV-1..INV-12 as a dict) plus SystemView (a read-only snapshot) and audit(view). audit runs 8 _CHECKS covering only INV-1,2,3,4,5,6,7 — the state-checkable ones. Any non-empty return is ALWAYS an incident. Note the TWO INV-1 checks: _check_cap (ceiling) and _check_budget_reconciliation (committed cents must equal sum of GRANT event amounts — catches CAS-without-append divergence).

Frozen dataclasses, all fail-closed in __post_init__: Money (integer cents, rejects float/bool/negative via FailClosedError), Organ, Proposal, Verdict, EvidencePack (HITL evidence pack, all-optional), BudgetState (carries version CAS token; __post_init__ enforces committed<=cap), Mode(SHADOW/LIVE), ProposalKind(GRANT/EFFECT/SPAWN), RevenueState (five states; FITNESS_COUNTABLE={CONFIRMED,ATTRIBUTED}), ExternalText.quarantined() (INV-9 delimiter wrap), GateDecision (allowed/reason/invariant/shadow/checks).

The three pure decision functions — the enforcement primitives (INV-4). budget_gate (admission vs cap), spawn_gate (depth<=1 + sigma), effector_gate (THE choke primitive). effector_gate ORDER is load-bearing: kill(INV-3) -> human verdict(INV-2, required for irreversible OR spawn) -> mode. Gates never execute; they return GateDecision.

Pure budget arithmetic under one cap (INV-1): headroom/reserve/release. Every derived state bumps version for optimistic-lock CAS at the store. Docstring explicitly flags this as 'load-bearing, do not simplify away' (v0.1 double-spend bug class).

Append-only hash-chained ledger 'the genome': EventKind enum, canonical_json (sort_keys, ensure_ascii=False so Persian/unicode survives), compute_hash (body format seq|ts|kind|json|prev_hash is a wire contract — changing it invalidates every existing chain), next_event (PURE — caller supplies ts, kernel never reads a clock), verify_chain (detects gap/reorder/forge). GENESIS_HASH = 64 zeros.

Branching-ratio population control (INV-6). CRITICAL distinction: sigma_from_events (current) vs prospective_sigma_from_events (value AFTER one more spawn). The gate must judge the prospective value or population overshoots the limit by one. sigma_allows_spawn is inclusive (sigma<=1.0). SIGMA_LIMIT=1.0.

Darwinian fitness from the ledger (INV-7/INV-8): reads only CONFIRMED/ATTRIBUTED revenue, never self-reports. Three-bucket spend (input/output/orchestration_cents) — orchestration is the easily-dropped bucket that silently poisons efficiency. FitnessReport.efficiency edge case: zero spend + positive value -> 1.0, zero/zero -> 0.0.

Allostatic pulse: epoch length as a pure clamped function of pressure (spend_velocity+deadline+anomaly), factor in [0.25,4.0], 2x base at rest. 'Heart is not a clock' — inputs modulate rhythm, never phase; no hidden state.

Lifecycle FSM (INV-10): ACTIVE<->THROTTLED<->DORMANT->EXTINCT. transition() enforces one-rung-at-a-time, EXTINCT absorbing and human-only (raises IllegalTransitionError / HumanVerdictRequiredError). This is where INV-10 lives structurally (not audit-checked).

The Protocols that are the ONLY doorway out: LLMPort, LedgerStore, BudgetStore (compare_and_swap contract, TOCTOU-safe), Telemetry, Clock, IdGen, KillSwitch (engage() must flip the REAL switch, not just ledger). Kernel never imports an adapter; app wires them.

Invariant-tagged error taxonomy: each KernelError subclass carries a .invariant string (CapExceeded=INV-1, HumanVerdictRequired=INV-2, Killed=INV-3, LedgerIntegrity=INV-5, SpawnViolation=INV-6, IllegalTransition=INV-10, FailClosed=INV-12). ConcurrencyConflictError.invariant is None on purpose — it is a retry signal, not a breach.

The Phase-0 architecture gate. AST-parses (does NOT execute) every module: kernel must be stdlib-only + import only itself; kernel must not import adapters/app/api; adapters must not import app/api. This test is the machine enforcing kernel purity — run it after any kernel edit.

NOT kernel, but essential context: ControlPlaneService.execute is the ACTUAL single runtime execution choke point (INV-4). It calls the pure effector_gate then does all the impure work the kernel refuses to: RLock, CAS retries, idempotency set (self._executed), saga-compensation on GRANT append failure, stale-approval TTL refusal, run_audit(). A new agent must keep this orchestration OUT of the kernel.

entry_points: The kernel has no runtime entry point — it is a pure library; nothing in it does I/O, reads the clock, reads env, or imports third-party code.

Conceptual enforcement primitive: kernel/gates.py::effector_gate — the pure choke that every world-touching action's decision passes through (invoked by app/service.py::ControlPlaneService.execute, the real orchestration choke).
Runtime conscience: kernel/invariants.py::audit(SystemView) — re-checks state-verifiable invariants; called from ControlPlaneService.run_audit() and trip_breaker_if_unsafe().
Integrity check: kernel/events.py::verify_chain(events) — validates the hash-chained ledger; used by _check_chain inside audit.
Fail-closed validation happens in the frozen-dataclass __post_init__ constructors (Money, Proposal, Verdict, BudgetState, Organ) — construction IS the gate for malformed input.
Test entry: pytest tests/l0_kernel + tests/test_import_lint.py (100 tests, all green here); full repo suite is 207.
rules_or_invariants: Kernel is stdlib-only, forever (INV-2 of CLAUDE.md / tests/test_import_lint.py). No third-party import, no I/O, no time.now(), no os.environ, no imports of adapters/app/api. Dependency direction is strictly kernel<-adapters<-app<-api.

Gates and all kernel functions are PURE: they take a snapshot, return a value/GateDecision, raise a tagged error — they never execute a side effect. All effects live behind ports.py Protocols, wired by the app layer.

Money is integer cents everywhere; a float or bool near the ledger is a defect. Every amount that could be adversarial is routed through Money() so it fails closed (Money rejects bool because bool subclasses int).

The ledger is append-only and hash-chained; history is never mutated. compute_hash's body format 'seq|ts|kind|canonical_json|prev_hash' and canonical_json's serialization are a persistence contract — altering either forges/invalidates every existing chain.

INV-11 / IMPROVE-DON'T-REWRITE: never edit, renumber, weaken, or delete an invariant; only add INV-13+ with the owner's explicit permission. The INVARIANTS dict must stay exactly 12 and sequentially numbered (tests assert both). The system never edits its own gates/policy.
Fail closed (INV-12): on unknown/invalid/missing input, deny and raise, never guess. Gates return a denial with the invariant tag; constructors raise FailClosedError.
Human sovereignty (INV-2): irreversible actions AND every spawn require an approved matching Verdict; self-reports are never sufficient (INV-8). Extinction is human-only and absorbing (INV-10).
BudgetState.version + BudgetStore.compare_and_swap is the anti-double-spend primitive; reserve/release bump version. Do not remove or 'simplify' the version/CAS discipline.
Spawn admissibility judges PROSPECTIVE sigma (after one more spawn), inclusive of 1.0; population is frozen when sigma>1 and depth is capped at 1 (INV-6).
Fitness counts only CONFIRMED/ATTRIBUTED revenue (FITNESS_COUNTABLE); spend accounting must include the orchestration_cents bucket.
gotchas: audit() does NOT cover all 12 invariants — only the 7 state-checkable ones (INV-1,2,3,4,5,6,7) via _CHECKS. INV-8/9/10/11/12 are enforced STRUCTURALLY at their definition sites (gates, domain __post_init__, lifecycle FSM, the import-lint test). A green audit does not mean every invariant holds. To add a new state-checkable invariant you add a _check_* fn to the _CHECKS tuple.

The 'one execution choke point' (ControlPlaneService.execute) is in the APP layer, not the kernel. The kernel only provides the pure effector_gate. All the impure machinery — RLock serialization, MAX_CAS_RETRIES, idempotency (self._executed keyed on the genome so it survives a soma rebuild), saga compensation (_compensate_release when a GRANT CAS commits but the event append fails), stale-approval TTL refusal — lives in service.py. Do not migrate any of it into the kernel.
effector_gate's check order is load-bearing: kill (INV-3) FIRST, then human verdict (INV-2), then mode. Reordering silently weakens safety (e.g., a killed system could be asked for a verdict first).

sigma has two nearly-identical functions: sigma_from_events (current) and prospective_sigma_from_events (+1). The gate/service must use the prospective one for admission and re-check, or the population overshoots the cap by one before freezing. sigma_allows_spawn is <= (1.0 is allowed).
FitnessReport.efficiency: zero spend with positive value returns 1.0 (float(True)); zero spend with zero value returns 0.0 — a deliberate, non-obvious edge case, not a bug.
canonical_json uses ensure_ascii=False so unicode (the project's Persian text) is preserved verbatim in the hash body; assume the hash is byte-sensitive to encoding.

audit's INV-1 is double-guarded: cap ceiling AND ledger reconciliation (committed must equal the summed GRANT event amounts). A CAS that lands without its GRANT append (or vice-versa) is caught here as 'ledger divergence' — this is why the saga-compensation in service.py exists.

SystemView.live_effects_executed / post_kill_executions are computed by the caller (service.run_audit does a single pass over events, and only passes live_effects when in SHADOW mode); the kernel check trusts those precomputed counters. If a future caller builds a SystemView, it must populate these correctly or the INV-3/INV-4 checks become blind.
Minor: invariants.py imports `field` from dataclasses but does not use it (harmless dead import).

Money.sub / BudgetState refuse to go negative (FailClosedError), so release() past committed and reserve() of <=0 both raise rather than clamp — callers must expect exceptions, not saturating arithmetic.
surveys.status: Stable and green — v0.2. Kernel + import-lint = 100 tests, all passing (verified by running pytest tests/l0_kernel tests/test_import_lint.py); repo-wide suite is 207 green. Kernel is stdlib-pure (import-lint enforced). No TODOs or dead code of substance in the kernel beyond one unused `field` import in invariants.py. The kernel is the settled foundation; active/unbuilt work (per MEMORY + docs/SECOND-BRAIN-SUPERGOVERNOR-v0.2.md) is at the layer above (B6 Second Brain), not here.

surveys.one_liner: The adapters layer is "everything that touches the world" — concrete implementations of the kernel's Protocol ports (LLMPort, LedgerStore, BudgetStore, Telemetry, Clock, IdGen, KillSwitch), chosen and wired exclusively at the app composition root (app/bootstrap.py); the kernel never imports them and they never import app/api, an invariant proven by an AST gate.

key_files.role: The contracts. Every adapter implements one of these @runtime Protocols. Docstring rule: keep ports minimal ('a fat port is lock-in wearing a trench coat'); the LLM adapter must fit behind LLMPort without leaking HTTP/graph types into the kernel.

The ONLY place adapters are selected/wired. build_llm() maps llm_mode->{MockLLM|ReplayLLM|FuguLLM}; build_service() chooses memory vs sqlite stores and injects clock/idgen/kill/telemetry into ControlPlaneService. Adapters are chosen here, nowhere else.

MemoryLedgerStore + MemoryBudgetStore. Explicitly the reference implementation whose semantics sqlite/Postgres must match: append-only ledger, atomic CAS on BudgetState.version, threading.Lock guards so threaded tests hit real races.

SqliteLedgerStore + SqliteBudgetStore (stdlib sqlite3, WAL). Encodes the two v0.1 bug classes: optimistic lock = single UPDATE ... WHERE version=? (rowcount!=1 -> ConcurrencyConflictError); TOCTOU-safe ledger append via BEGIN IMMEDIATE + UNIQUE(seq) + UNIQUE(hash).

FuguLLM — OpenAI-compatible Sakana 'fugu' adapter, stdlib urllib only, frozen dataclass with injected key/host/model. The security centerpiece: a module-level no-redirect opener plus one all-encompassing parse guard, fails closed as FuguError (subclass of FailClosedError/INV-12) on any error.

RecordingLLM (wraps a live port, appends JSONL keyed by sha256(task\x00prompt)) and ReplayLLM (answers from cassette only, raises CassetteMissError on missing file/corrupt line/unrecorded request). The L2 test backbone; a miss is a drifted test, never a mock fallback.
MockLLM — deterministic sha256-derived echo. The dependency-free baseline brain (no network, no keys). Default llm_mode.

VaultScanner — READ-ONLY Obsidian markdown analysis (Phase 2). Builds a wikilink graph, finds orphans, infers cross-folder channels with confidence+risk. Resolve-based exclusion of restricted folders; writes nothing to the vault.

SystemClock/UuidGen/FileKillSwitch (production) plus FixedClock/SequentialIdGen/ManualKillSwitch (test doubles co-located in the same module). FileKillSwitch = a file existing; touchable by any human/cron.
NoopTelemetry (production no-op, Phase 3 swaps OTel behind the same port) + CapturingTelemetry (in-memory test tap).

AppConfig.from_env — the only reader of env/.env. Adapters get their config values from here via bootstrap, never directly. Includes the UTF-8-BOM .env footgun fix and the SHADOW/NBB_ALLOW_LIVE fail-closed gate.

The AST architecture gate (17 tests). Proves kernel is stdlib-only and enforces kernel<-adapters<-app<-api direction: adapters may import only kernel+adapters. Catches 3 relative/absolute import spellings that previously bypassed the check.
Parametrized memory+sqlite contract tests (14). Asserts conservation (committed == landed*amount, not the tautological committed<=cap) and that 4 concurrent writers never fork ledger history.

entry_points: app/bootstrap.py::build_service(config, in_memory=False) — composition root; the one function that instantiates and injects every adapter into ControlPlaneService
app/bootstrap.py::build_llm(config) -> LLMPort — selects MockLLM / ReplayLLM / FuguLLM from config.llm_mode ('mock'|'cassette'|'fugu'|'live')
app/service.py::ControlPlaneService.execute — the single execution choke point (INV-4) that actually consumes the wired ledger/budget/kill/telemetry adapters
kernel/ports.py — the Protocol definitions an adapter must satisfy to be pluggable
adapters/vault/scanner.py::VaultScanner.scan() — standalone read-only entry (not wired into the service; produces a ScanResult / channel-map markdown)
rules_or_invariants: Adapters implement kernel Protocols and may import ONLY kernel + adapters — never app or api (enforced by tests/test_import_lint.py::TestDependencyDirection). Dependency direction kernel<-adapters<-app<-api is a hard gate.

Adapters never read config or env. All dependency values (fugu api_key/host/model, db_path, cassette_path, kill file) are injected from the app layer via bootstrap. FuguLLM is a frozen dataclass; AppConfig.from_env is the sole env reader.

Fail closed everywhere (CLAUDE.md rule 4 / INV-12): ReplayLLM raises CassetteMissError on any miss (never a mock fallback); FuguLLM raises FuguError on any API/parse error; build_llm raises on unknown llm_mode or missing key; config forces SHADOW on unknown NBB_MODE and requires NBB_ALLOW_LIVE=1 for live. Both CassetteMissError and FuguError subclass FailClosedError so the service handles them uniformly.

Budget CAS must be atomic: a single UPDATE ... WHERE id=1 AND version=? with rowcount!=1 -> ConcurrencyConflictError. Never a two-step read-modify-write (the TOCTOU lesson, stated in ports.py BudgetStore docstring).

Ledger is append-only and hash-chained. sqlite enforces it structurally with BEGIN IMMEDIATE + UNIQUE(seq) + UNIQUE(hash), so even an upstream bug cannot silently fork history. verify_chain detects any gap/forgery.
Money is integer cents throughout; no float near the ledger. sqlite stores cap_cents/committed as INTEGER.

VaultScanner is strictly read-only and must never write to the vault (asserted by test_scan_writes_nothing comparing byte content before/after). Restricted folders (People, Telegram, Crypto-etoro) excluded by default unless include_restricted=True.

Kernel stays stdlib-only; the only third-party dependency permitted anywhere near the kernel boundary is confined to adapters (fugu uses stdlib urllib specifically to keep the whole package dependency-free; LangGraph, if added, lives only under adapters/llm/).
gotchas: FuguLLM._NoRedirect is a deliberate key-exfiltration guard, not boilerplate. stdlib urllib re-sends 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' to a 3xx redirect target with NO same-host check, so a redirect from a compromised/MITM'd endpoint would leak the key (cleartext if http://). The module-level _OPENER = build_opener(_NoRedirect) refuses ALL redirects. TRAP: tests must patch fugu._OPENER.open, NOT urllib.request.urlopen, or they bypass the guard entirely.

sqlite's stored payload TEXT is NOT the hashed representation. sqlite.py writes payload via json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True) (spaced separators) but the hash comes from compute_hash -> canonical_json (compact separators). This is correct because verify_chain recomputes the hash from the PARSED dict via canonical_json and JSON round-trips preserve the dict. Corollary trap: tuples in a payload become JSON lists on sqlite reload (memory store keeps tuples) yet hashes still match across stores because canonical_json serializes both identically. Do not 'fix' the serialization to match — it would not change the hash and could destabilize cross-store equivalence assumptions.

VaultScanner exclusion is resolve-based on purpose: it does path.resolve().relative_to(root.resolve()) so a symlink/junction pointing into a restricted folder is still excluded and a link escaping the vault is skipped (test_symlink_into_restricted_is_excluded). And risk is computed from the FULL real paths, not the collapsed top-level folder — otherwise a crypto note (whose folder collapses '03 - Projects/Crypto - etoro' -> '03 - Projects') would be mislabeled 'medium' instead of 'critical' (test_crypto_note_makes_channel_critical). Both are regression-guarded correctness traps.

Everything touching the Fugu 200 body — including usage/token extraction — is inside ONE try/except. A malformed-but-200 response (non-dict usage, non-numeric tokens, missing content, invalid UTF-8 bytes) fails closed as FuguError rather than raising a raw AttributeError/ValueError that would bypass ControlPlaneService's incident handler. Keep new parsing inside that guard.

Two different 'live' concepts that are easy to conflate: (a) llm_mode='live' in build_llm is just an ALIAS for 'fugu' (builds FuguLLM); (b) Mode.LIVE (execution mode) is gated separately in config.from_env, which forces SHADOW unless NBB_ALLOW_LIVE=1. Confusing them could accidentally enable live effects.

Test doubles live INSIDE the production adapter modules by design: FixedClock, SequentialIdGen, ManualKillSwitch (runtime/system.py), CapturingTelemetry (telemetry/noop.py). They ship behind the same ports intentionally — do not 'clean them up' into tests/; that would be a rewrite touching a module's public surface (IMPROVE-DON'T-REWRITE).

SqliteLedgerStore.read_all() takes the store lock even for pure reads — deliberate, because a sqlite3 connection resets pending cursors on commit/rollback and unsynchronized cross-thread reads can observe truncated results (comment in code). Side effect: head() calls read_all() and materializes the whole table each time — O(n) per head()/snapshot() call, a known Phase-2 perf item, not a bug.

_load_dotenv reads with encoding='utf-8-sig' specifically to strip a Windows/PowerShell UTF-8 BOM; without it the first key parses as '﻿FUGU_API_KEY' and the API key is silently dropped. A real Windows footgun that was already fixed — don't revert it.

FileKillSwitch semantics: engage() writes 'engaged\n', engaged() == path.exists(), release() == unlink(missing_ok=True). record_kill in the service engages the real switch FIRST, then ledgers KILL (safety over bookkeeping) so the API's only stop control actually halts every gate rather than writing an event the effector gate never reads. Default kill file is outputs/KILL.

The memory and sqlite stores are behavior twins verified by a single parametrized fixture; memory is documented as the canonical contract spec. When adding the Phase-2 Postgres twin, it must pass the identical test_stores_concurrency.py contract (append-only + atomic CAS + conservation), not a relaxed one.
surveys.status: Complete and green: 207 tests pass (confirmed via pytest --collect-only). All seven ports have production adapters plus co-located test doubles. FuguLLM (Phase-3 live brain) is fully implemented and fail-closed but reachable only behind llm_mode=fugu/live + FUGU_API_KEY. Known deferred/TODO items visible in docstrings: a Postgres twin of the storage ports behind the same ports (Phase 2), OTel telemetry replacing NoopTelemetry (Phase 3), and completing api/http.py validation/status codes (Phase 4). VaultScanner is complete and read-only but its ScanResult/channel-map is NOT yet wired into any B6 ActionProposal flow — that owner-approval path is future work. No adapter currently imports any third-party package (fugu deliberately uses stdlib urllib), preserving the dependency-free invariant.

surveys.subsystem: app (src/nbb_cp/app) — the orchestration layer: ControlPlaneService, StubGovernor, bootstrap wiring, and config/env loading.
surveys.one_liner: The app layer is the organism's heart: ControlPlaneService.execute is the single choke point every effect passes through, backed by an append-only genome (ledger) with disposable soma projections, fail-closed everywhere, wired to adapters only in bootstrap.py.

key_files.role: ControlPlaneService — THE one execution path (26KB, the heart). Public API: submit_proposal, record_verdict, execute, record_revenue, record_spend, record_kill, resume, advance_epoch, sigma, fitness, snapshot, run_audit, trip_breaker_if_unsafe, rebuild_projections. Holds genome (ledger, authoritative) vs soma (_proposals/_verdicts/_executed, rebuildable). RLock serializes TOCTOU windows. Idempotency via _executed. Saga compensation in _execute_grant. Approval-TTL staleness in _approval_is_stale.

StubGovernor (deterministic allocation planner behind LLMPort) + run_demo_epoch (one scripted plan->propose->execute->account->advance epoch). Governor only PROPOSES (INV-4). MAX_GRANT_CENTS=500; stub prices 1 token = 1 cent. Docstring says Phase 1 will swap the stub for a LangGraph agent keeping this exact call surface.

build_service / build_llm — the ONLY place adapters are chosen. build_llm maps mock->MockLLM, cassette->ReplayLLM, fugu|live->FuguLLM (fails closed if key absent). build_service picks Memory vs Sqlite stores via in_memory flag, wires SystemClock/UuidGen/FileKillSwitch/NoopTelemetry.

AppConfig frozen dataclass + from_env + _load_dotenv. Merges gitignored .env (fills gaps) then os.environ (real env wins). Contains the M5 live gate (NBB_MODE=live clamped to shadow unless NBB_ALLOW_LIVE=1) and unknown-mode->shadow clamp. FUGU_* fields; fugu_model default 'fugu' (standard tier, not ultra).

Pure decision functions the app calls: budget_gate (GRANT admission vs global cap), spawn_gate (SPAWN population discipline INV-6), effector_gate (the choke-point rule: kill INV-3 -> human sovereignty INV-2 -> mode). App enforces idempotency + TTL staleness ON TOP of effector_gate.

Protocols the app depends on and bootstrap satisfies: LLMPort, LedgerStore (append-only), BudgetStore (compare_and_swap on version — the anti-double-spend primitive), Telemetry, Clock, IdGen, KillSwitch.

The only direct app-layer unit test file surveyed: pins from_env's mode fail-closed clamp, the M5 live gate, .env loading incl. UTF-8 BOM handling, real-env-wins-over-dotenv, and Fugu key read. Note comment: from_env previously had zero coverage (a review finding).

entry_points: ControlPlaneService.execute(proposal_id) — the single execution choke point; everything touching the world passes effector_gate here under self._lock (service.py:187).
ControlPlaneService.submit_proposal(...) — intake; admits through the per-kind gate and ledgers a PROPOSAL event, never executes (service.py:95).
app.bootstrap.build_service(config, in_memory=False) — constructs the fully-wired service; build_llm(config) selects the LLM adapter (bootstrap.py:38, :19).
app.config.AppConfig.from_env(env=None) — the env/.env -> config boundary, incl. the M5 live gate (config.py:54).
app.governor.run_demo_epoch(service, llm) — the scripted governance loop used by L2 replay tests and run.py (governor.py:70).
rules_or_invariants: ONE choke point (INV-4 / CLAUDE.md rule 3): every GRANT/SPAWN/EFFECT effect flows through ControlPlaneService.execute -> effector_gate. A second execution path is a defect. submit_proposal/record_verdict deliberately NEVER execute.

Genome vs soma: the ledger is the sole authority; _proposals/_verdicts/_executed are disposable projections. rebuild_projections() recreates them (and restores _current_epoch = max epoch) purely from the ledger — called even in __init__, so state is always genome-derived.

Idempotency (INV-2): one admission + one verdict authorize EXACTLY ONE execution. _executed is keyed on the genome, so the refusal survives a soma rebuild/restart. A replay ledgers an INCIDENT and returns denied; it never re-runs. Denials do NOT consume the key (stay retryable).

Fail closed everywhere (rule 4): unknown organ/mode/proposal -> deny + INCIDENT; Money() rejects negative/float amounts (INV-8/INV-12); build_llm raises FailClosedError rather than falling back to a mock; unknown NBB_MODE -> shadow.

Money is integer cents end-to-end (rule 5). record_spend/record_revenue route every bucket through Money so an adversarial LLM self-reporting negative tokens fails closed at the ledger boundary, not by inflating fitness.

Dependency direction kernel<-adapters<-app<-api: config.py docstring states 'the kernel never sees this module'; adapters are imported ONLY in bootstrap.py. The app imports kernel gates/ports/domain, never the reverse.

Kill-first ordering (INV-3): record_kill engages the real switch BEFORE ledgering KILL (safety over bookkeeping); resume ledgers RESUME BEFORE releasing (a failed release leaves the system safely stopped).

Budget two-store atomicity (INV-1): reservations land via compare_and_swap with MAX_CAS_RETRIES=5; if CAS commits but the GRANT event fails to append, _compensate_release rolls the reservation back (saga compensation) so committed budget can never silently diverge from the genome.

Human sovereignty + TTL (INV-2): SPAWN and irreversible proposals require an approved matching verdict; additionally an approval aged past proposal.approval_ttl_epochs is refused as stale, requiring a fresh human verdict.
M5 live gate (SPEC §6): NBB_MODE=live is clamped to shadow unless NBB_ALLOW_LIVE=1 is set explicitly — execution mode is unreachable-by-default until the Phase-6 shadow-to-live gate.
gotchas: TWO independent 'live' concepts, easy to conflate. (1) execution `mode` (Mode.LIVE) is gated by NBB_ALLOW_LIVE=1. (2) `llm_mode` ('live'/'fugu') is NOT gated — setting NBB_LLM_MODE=fugu with a key present calls the real Sakana API even while execution stays in shadow. By design (planning always calls the LLM; shadow only simulates OUTWARD effects), but a next agent could hit a paid live endpoint thinking shadow means no-op.

Docs/comments say LangGraph, the code ships Fugu. config.py's llm_mode comment and .env.example describe the third mode as 'live = real provider via the LangGraph adapter', and governor.py's docstring still says 'Phase 1 replaces the stub with a real LangGraph agent'. But bootstrap.build_llm actually maps both 'fugu' and 'live' to FuguLLM (Sakana OpenAI-compatible). Naming drift — trust the code.

Budget reservation is REAL in shadow mode. _execute_grant commits the reservation via CAS in BOTH modes (internal bookkeeping); only the outward effect is simulated (decision.shadow). So committed_cents/headroom move even in shadow — do NOT 'fix' this thinking shadow should leave budget untouched.

The service RLock guards ONLY execute, record_kill, resume, advance_epoch, trip_breaker_if_unsafe. submit_proposal and record_verdict are intentionally unlocked (they aren't part of a check-then-append TOCTOU window). Any future concurrent-submission feature must re-examine this.

organ-level SPENDs from record_spend carry NO proposal_id, so rebuild_projections skips them when reconstructing _executed. Only GRANT/SPAWN and effect-SPEND (which DO carry proposal_id) mark a proposal as executed. Don't add a proposal_id to accounting SPENDs without thinking about idempotency replay.
run_audit's live_effects_executed only counts as a violation when self._mode is Mode.SHADOW (else forced to 0). The audit's meaning of 'live effect leaked' is mode-relative.

trip_breaker_if_unsafe is an opt-in circuit breaker and is NOT auto-wired to any path — normal operation is unchanged until a caller (e.g. a governor loop) invokes it. Don't assume the breaker fires automatically.

The worktree .env contains a real-looking FUGU_API_KEY value (fish_...). It is gitignored per CLAUDE.md rule 6, but it is present on disk — never commit it, echo it into the ledger/cassette, or sync it to backups. rules_or_invariants: Status discipline is the API's whole job: 201 create / 200 read+verdict+execute / 409 gate-denial / 422 invalid body / 404 unknown-proposal. Gate denials must never surface as 500.
GET /audit must never 500 on findings — it returns 200 with {"violations":[...]} (empty list when clean). Audit findings are data, not errors.

Gate-denial bodies are structured and cite the invariant: FastAPI nests them so the wire shape is {"detail": {"reason":..., "invariant":...}} (tests read response.json()['detail']['invariant'], e.g. 'INV-1').

The API is a pure translation layer over ControlPlaneService.execute — the single execution choke point (INV-4). It must not add a second path to any effect; all it does is map return values / FailClosedError to HTTP.

FastAPI is an optional extra (pip install -e .[api]). Nothing in kernel/adapters/app imports this module, so the kernel-stdlib-only invariant and the kernel<-adapters<-app<-api dependency direction stay intact. Importing http.py without fastapi raises a deliberate, clear ImportError.

/kill and /resume take `by` as a QUERY parameter (FastAPI scalar-with-default convention), not a JSON body — test calls client.post('/kill', params={'by':'armin'}). Easy to get wrong when adding a client or the dashboard.
gotchas: FailClosedError is OVERLOADED across routes: create_proposal maps it to 422 (invalid input), but record_verdict and execute map the SAME exception type to 404 (unknown/unadmitted proposal). The status is route-specific, not exception-specific — because the service reuses FailClosedError for 'unknown proposal' too. Don't assume FailClosedError == 422.

The pydantic `kind` regex ^(grant|effect|spawn)$ (http.py:35) must stay hand-synced with the ProposalKind enum. Junk kinds are rejected at the pydantic layer (422) BEFORE the service. If that regex ever drifts, ProposalKind(body.kind) at http.py:74 would raise a bare ValueError — which is NOT caught by the `except FailClosedError` and would leak as a 500. It's only safe today because the regex guards it first.

execute is NOT idempotent-at-200: re-POSTing execute on an already-executed proposal returns 409 (decision INV-2 'already executed'), and the service logs an INCIDENT + emits nbb.execution.replay_refused. The idempotency key lives in the service (self._executed, rebuilt from the genome), keyed so it survives a soma rebuild/restart. A retry is refused, never re-run.

POST /proposals is NOT idempotent yet — a client retry double-ledgers a PROPOSAL event. Service-level idempotency only guards execute. Phase-4 item 'Idempotency keys on POST /proposals' is explicitly still open.

There is no server entrypoint and no composition root. api/__init__.py is empty, uvicorn is a declared dependency but imported nowhere, and there is no module-level `app` or service builder. You cannot `uvicorn nbb_cp.api.http:app` — someone must first construct a ControlPlaneService (with ledger/budget/llm/clock/idgen/kill/organs) and call create_app(service). Wiring that composition root is unbuilt work.

Read surface is minimal: only GET /state (full snapshot) and GET /audit exist. No ledger paging, organs, fitness, or sigma endpoints yet (Phase 4). GET /health also returns a `killed` field that the module-header docstring contract doesn't list — minor doc drift.

No authentication and no rate limiting exist. Every mutating route (proposals/verdict/execute/kill/resume) is open. The single-operator-token stub and rate limit are Phase-4 deferred, so do not treat this as deployable as-is.

In shadow mode (the default) a successful execute returns 200 with simulated:true; the effect is ledgered but not performed. A caller that reads 200 as 'the real-world effect happened' is wrong until NBB_MODE=live — the effector_gate decides shadow vs live, not the API.

Tests assert the SPECIFIC invariant id (decision.invariant == 'INV-N') and frequently the reason string ('expired', 'divergence', 'drifted', 'corrupt', 'not found', 'forged'), never just a bare 'denied' — a new agent must preserve those identifiers and messages.

CODING_AGENT_PROMPT.md prescribes the mandatory reading order for any continuing agent: (1) docs/SPEC_v0.2.md, (2) src/nbb_cp/kernel/invariants.py (the law itself, cited by ID), (3) docs/ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md, (4) CODING_AGENT_PROMPT.md fully before writing code.

rules_or_invariants: INVARIANTS ARE SACRED (INV-11): never delete, renumber, or weaken an invariant; you may only ADD INV-13+ with the owner's approval. If a phase requirement conflicts with an invariant, the invariant wins — you STOP and report, you do not 'temporarily' disable it.

kernel/ stays pure stdlib-only (proven by tests/test_import_lint.py). Dependency direction is kernel <- adapters <- app <- api/ui, NEVER reversed. Any LLM library (LangGraph, Fugu) lives only inside adapters/llm/; a graph/provider type in a kernel or app signature breaks the contract.
ONE choke point: every effect flows through ControlPlaneService.execute (INV-4). Adding a second execution path is a defect — stop.

FAIL CLOSED everywhere (INV-12): unknown state => shadow/deny + ledger an INCIDENT + stop. Cassette miss = error, never a mock fallback. Unknown mode => shadow. Unknown organ/revenue-state => raise, don't guess.

Money is integer cents end-to-end; a float near the ledger is a defect. There is exactly ONE cap: NBB_GLOBAL_CAP_CENTS; a second number that must 'agree' with it is a future bug (the '100 vs 30' lesson).
Secrets never enter the repo, ledger, or cassettes; scrub recorded traffic and forbid sk--like patterns in commits (CLAUDE.md rule 6).
If a decision is NOT derivable from spec + invariants, STOP and ask the human — guessing on 'the law' is INV-12 territory.

Suite always green: new behavior ships with its test in the SAME commit; a bug => write the regression test first; do NOT refactor across phase boundaries 'while you're there' (note it in the report instead).

IMPROVE, DON'T REWRITE: add capability BESIDE the old (versioning), keep the previous version (deletion needs explicit owner approval), never change an existing interface or externally-observable behavior. Rewrite triggers requiring a stop-and-ask: >~30% of a module's logic changes, any interface change, >1 capability changing at once, an old version deleted, or final output behavior changing. Before ANY change show Current / Delta / Preserved / Rollback.

PHASE DISCIPLINE: execute phases in order, never start a phase before the prior gate is GREEN, stop after each phase, fill the mandatory report template, and await a human verdict. 'Green' means the actual command output, not a claim — INV-8 (self-reports untrusted) applies to the agent itself; self-reporting without evidence is rejected.

SECOND BRAIN DATA-SAFETY SPINE: nothing touches restricted folders (09-People, Crypto-etoro, 10-Telegram, Accounting, OnlyFans) without per-phase owner approval AND passing through B6 as ActionProposal -> gate -> human verdict -> ledger. Shadow-first always; live is unreachable until the SPEC §6 / Phase-6 shadow-to-live gate; each sensitive action class is enabled individually.
gotchas: TEST-COUNT DRIFT is real and the count is deliberately NOT a gate. Docs say 150 (SPEC_v0.2, CODING_AGENT_PROMPT Phase 0, SKELETON_HARDENING, ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW) or 171 (SECOND-BRAIN-BUILD-PLAN); the task states 207; the tree currently has ~189 `def test_` (some parametrized). ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW §2 explicitly decided 'the gate is all-green, not a count.' Do NOT edit docs to make numbers match, and do NOT treat any count as a gate.

Git log shows Second Brain Phases 1-3 already done (second-brain/ prompts+templates, scripts/scan_vault.py, adapters/vault/, a live Fugu/Sakana adapter), plus evidence pack + approval TTL, execute() idempotency + grant saga compensation, live gate, and CI — yet SPEC_v0.2 / CODING_AGENT_PROMPT / SKELETON_HARDENING still narrate the raw skeleton with those items 'deferred.' SKELETON_HARDENING's deferred H1/M2/M5/H6 have since been at least partly addressed. Verify status against git + code, never trust the doc prose's status lines.

TWO PARALLEL, UNRECONCILED ROADMAPS. CODING_AGENT_PROMPT.md's 8-phase NBB-CP roadmap has Phase 1 = 'real LLM via LangGraph adapter', but the actual build followed SECOND-BRAIN-BUILD-PLAN.md instead and wired Fugu/Sakana (OpenAI-compatible) behind LLMPort — LangGraph was NEVER used. An agent handed CODING_AGENT_PROMPT.md alone would wrongly conclude it is at 'Phase 0 baseline' and start building a LangGraph adapter. The LangGraph-containment RULE still holds; the LangGraph deliverable does not.

TWO DIFFERENT SYSTEMS are easy to conflate. NBB Control Plane = BUILT (it IS component B6). Second Brain Super-Governor (SECOND-BRAIN-SUPERGOVERNOR-v0.2.md) = SPEC only, marked 'هنوز ساخته نشده' (not built). SECOND-BRAIN-BUILD-PLAN.md's header still says 'PLAN ONLY, nothing built' even though git shows its Phases 1-3 executed — the header is stale.

CLAUDE.md's binding rules are in PERSIAN. The non-negotiable STRICT SAFETY RULES and the IMPROVE-DON'T-REWRITE short form are Persian text; English appears mainly in the docs/ bodies and tables. An agent that only skims English can miss the actual governing rules — read the Persian in CLAUDE.md.

A GREEN TEST IS NOT PROOF. SKELETON_HARDENING documents that the original '150 green' was 'partly dishonest': test_racing_reservations_never_exceed_cap was tautological (a broken CAS passed it) and the import-lint gate had 3 bypasses. Both were fixed AND mutation-tested (a broken impl now fails them). The standing lesson: any new safety-critical test must be mutation-checked — confirm a broken implementation actually fails it.

KNOWN-BUT-INTENTIONAL INCONSISTENCIES flagged as LOW in SKELETON_HARDENING should not be silently 'fixed': Organ.vital defaults True (every seeded organ is cull-exempt until the cull loop lands); INV-3's registry/.env wording ('every gate denies') is stricter than the code (only the effector gate denies); .env.example said 'copy to .env' though nothing originally loaded a dotenv (git later added key loading). Treat these as owner-decision items / proposals, not drive-by edits.

rules_or_invariants: B6 = this repo. IMPROVE-DON'T-REWRITE: NBB-CP is never rebuilt; new brains are 'config + prompt + a thin adapter', never new control logic. Any change >~30% of a module or any interface change = 'rewrite' -> stop and ask owner (CLAUDE.md).

One choke point: every effect goes through ControlPlaneService.execute (INV-4). The SuperBrain and all 8 brains only PROPOSE — can_execute:false in agents.yaml and SUPERBRAIN-GOVERNOR.md. A second execution path = defect.

8 gated action classes NEVER auto-execute; each becomes an ActionProposal -> B6 -> ALLOW/REVIEW/DENY/PAUSE/KILL: external_communication, financial, content_publish, architecture_mutation, code_execution, vault_mass_update, memory_promote, private_data_export.

Data-safety spine: nothing touches People / Crypto-eToro / Telegram / Accounting / OnlyFans without per-phase owner approval AND passing through B6 as proposal->verdict->ledger. Reads of restricted folders are opt-in per folder. Scanner's DEFAULT_RESTRICTED excludes them.
Shadow-first: every runtime phase runs in Mode.SHADOW (simulate + ledger, never execute) until the owner promotes a SPECIFIC action class; live is unreachable until the SPEC §6 / Phase-6 gate.

Memory ladder (spec §15): raw -> episodic -> semantic -> canonical_candidate -> (approval) -> canonical. No brain writes canonical directly; promotion is an evidence-gated proposal (policy no_canonical_without_evidence). status frontmatter must climb, never jump.

Kernel stays stdlib-only (tests/test_import_lint.py enforces). Dependency direction kernel<-adapters<-app<-api. The VaultScanner correctly lives in adapters/vault/ and is stdlib-only; the Fugu adapter lives in adapters/llm/. Fail-closed everywhere; cassette miss = error, never mock fallback.
Secrets never enter repo/ledger/cassette (CLAUDE.md rule 6). agents.yaml stores only api_key_env: FUGU_API_KEY (a name), never the value; the key is env/.env at runtime.
gotchas: BUILT vs PLANNED is subtler than the docs admit. Two different 'Governors' collide by name. The SuperBrain Governor (B0, intent router over 8 brains) is NOT built. app/governor.py StubGovernor is the pre-existing NBB organ-budget allocator (prices 1 token = 1 cent) and is unrelated. The Phase-3 SuperBrain router must be a NEW adapter behind LLMPort, not a modification of StubGovernor.

Scanner risk-labelling trap (documented in scanner.py _risk_from_paths): a note's top-level folder collapses subfolders, so '03 - Projects/Crypto - etoro' becomes '03 - Projects'. Risk MUST be judged from full note PATHS, not collapsed folder names, or a crypto channel is mislabeled 'medium' instead of 'critical'. Also, _read_notes resolves symlinks/junctions so a link from an included folder into a restricted one is still excluded and links escaping the vault are skipped (fail-closed).
